title: The Hiking Trip
acts: The trailhead sign-in sheet had barely dried before the group scattered to its factions. Aubrey, Brianna and Hank formed the self-appointed Windy Trail cap club, an alliance held together by nothing but matching headwear — Hank's a size too small, worn anyway on principle. Down on the Rocky Trail, Clark and Finlay had both shown up in sunglasses despite the overcast sky, which they took as proof they were meant to hike together. Danika peeled off toward the Pine Forest alone, the way she'd wanted the whole trip to go from the start. Gavin practically jogged for the Summit, one boot up on the first boulder he found like he'd personally put it there. Elias stayed behind in the Ranger's Hut fussing over waivers nobody had read, Iris settled into the Booth's one good chair with no intention of moving, and Kobe ducked into the Grove, his plaid shirt doing an unsettling amount of camouflage work.

Deeper in, at the edge of Bear Woods, Joe was telling Vincenza — headphones in, sunglasses on, gamely not listening to a word — that the bear everyone kept whispering about was "basically tame, honestly, barely worth mentioning." What nobody mentioned, and what the trail map certainly didn't, was that there were two real bears out there that day, each one quietly occupying a stretch of woods that should otherwise have been empty. Finlay, four rows further down the Rocky Trail than he had any idea, was one wrong turn from meeting his. Brianna kept pacing out her distance from Finlay like a woman doing sums, Clark matched him stride for stride, and back on the Windy Trail, Hank brought up the rear grumbling that it never used to take three people and a headcount to lose a footpath.

It was Elias, cross-checking his waiver list against the returning stragglers, who noticed the gap first: everyone back except Vincenza. And Joe, oddly, was already back too — freshly washed hands, no bear story to tell, and absolutely no headphones in sight.

whereabouts.A: Aubrey kept her cap pulled low against the wind, defending the Windy Trail cap club's honor against accusations that Hank's didn't count.
whereabouts.B: Brianna paced out her distance from Finlay in whole rows, treating the Windy Trail like a maths problem she refused to leave unsolved.
whereabouts.C: Clark kept his sunglasses on under an overcast sky, matching Finlay step for step down the Rocky Trail out of pure sunglasses solidarity.
whereabouts.D: Danika had gone alone into the Pine Forest, getting exactly the solitude she'd been angling for since the trailhead.
whereabouts.E: Elias stayed back in the Ranger's Hut, fussing over a waiver list nobody had actually read.
whereabouts.F: Finlay strolled the Rocky Trail beside Clark, four rows and one bad turn away from a bear he had no idea was there.
whereabouts.G: Gavin had already reached the Summit and was resting a boot on a boulder as though he'd personally hauled it up there.
whereabouts.H: Hank brought up the rear of the Windy Trail group, cap two sizes too small, muttering that it never used to take a committee to lose a footpath.
whereabouts.I: Iris had claimed the Booth's one good chair and made it extremely clear she wasn't giving it back.
whereabouts.J: Joe stood at the edge of Bear Woods reassuring Vincenza that the local bear was "basically tame," a claim nobody had asked him to make with such confidence.
whereabouts.K: Kobe had ducked into the Grove for shade, his plaid shirt blending into the undergrowth a little too well.
whereabouts.V: Vincenza wandered into Bear Woods with her headphones in and her sunglasses on, blissfully unaware of anyone, or anything, nearby.

reveal: It was Joe, in Bear Woods, and there was never any bear involved at all — that was the whole point of bringing one up. He'd picked the spot because a growl and a rustle in the right bushes bought him thirty uninterrupted seconds with someone who couldn't hear him coming or going. A fallen branch did the rest, and by the time Elias finished his headcount, Joe had already rinsed his hands in the nearest stream and rehearsed his very calm, very concerned face.

escape.generic: Somewhere out there, two actual bears are still getting blamed for something neither of them did, and the person who invented a third one is already back at the trailhead loading up the car.

byAccused.A: Aubrey was marched off still defending the honor of the Windy Trail cap club, insisting a matching hat is not a motive.
byAccused.B: Brianna went quietly, still two rows off from finishing whatever calculation she'd been running about Finlay.
byAccused.C: Clark kept his sunglasses on through the entire arrest, which the rangers agreed was deeply unsettling but not, on its own, a confession.
byAccused.D: Danika got the solitude she wanted after all, just with considerably more paperwork attached.
byAccused.E: Elias was hauled off mid-sentence about the waivers, which — everyone quietly agreed — really should have been read.
byAccused.F: Finlay never did find out how close he'd come to a real bear, which made getting arrested for a fake one feel especially unfair.
byAccused.G: Gavin was escorted down from the Summit still insisting the boulder incident had nothing to do with anything.
byAccused.H: Hank grumbled the entire way down that it never used to take this many people to arrest the wrong hiker either.
byAccused.I: Iris had to be talked out of the Booth's chair a second time, this time by someone with handcuffs.
byAccused.K: Kobe was pulled out of the Grove still wearing the plaid shirt that had nearly gotten him lost in it.
